restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte messages P || 0^32 || x and P || 0^32 || y (x != y, 256-bit little-endian integers), P the fixed 64-byte string of proof.md Section 8: one chunk of two blocks, block 1 = P (flags 1, counter 0, length 64), block 2 = 0^32 || x (flags 10, counter 0, length 64, chaining value = the chaining value of P), standard IV, unkeyed, the complete 256-bit digest of the 3-round hash (blake3-r3-prefix-v1), found as a collision f(x) = f(y) of f(x) = digest(P || 0^32 || x). Plain birthday attack; no differential or structural property of the 3 rounds is used. The two-block mode is declared as H4.

Machine, a premise of this entry: a classical load/store machine with 256-bit words, 256-bit immediates and 1,024 registers under collision-frontier-v5 (the profile fixes the word size and charges loads and stores, not a register count); 638 operations (C of blake3-r3) to the unit. Charged: every add, AND, OR, XOR, shift, compare, branch, register move, load, store and the random word. The main loop evaluates 256 trails bit-sliced: 18904 operations per batch (18866 gates and XORs with all-ones, a 35-operation stage-1 test, 3 loop operations) with no load, store or move; it needs 771 registers. Smaller files are priced in proof.md 3.5 (125.0227 at 512, 125.2382 at 256).

time_log2 is an upper bound: every term of proof.md Section 3.4 is enforced by a halt of the program (B batches, e2max stage-1 hits, 10160 table keys, 2 cut trails, a recovery of at most c + 2^48 batches, one recovery), and the bound charges each at its limit. The attempt is single: one fresh uniform 256-bit word r, no restart, no amplification, no stored collision; the advice is the prefix word i and the polarity vector PINS (two words, nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 6); m0..m7 of the last block = 0. Distinguished points: low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 142 (density 142 / 2^122).

Memory: 10160 table entries of 25 bytes (254000 bytes) plus 745344 bytes of code (20704 instructions of 36 bytes) plus 16,384 bytes of counters and the plane copy plus 32,768 bytes for the 1,024 registers plus the 64-byte advice (prefix word and polarity vector): 1048560 bytes <= 2^20; claimed as 2^20, so the memory term of the score is 0. The circuit generator that runs at setup is accounted in proof 3.6: 1600 instructions of code (57600 bytes) and a peak scratch of 222366 bytes, both held in the region that the table and the register file occupy once the search runs; the setup phase needs 1041758 bytes, the search phase 1048560.

Success probability at least 0.39 holds under H1 (proof.md Section 5) with the losses of Section 4 (about 4.37e-04 spent of 1.65e-03 available). If the pair-collision rate of the evaluated inputs were (1 - eps) of the random-mapping rate, the success probability stays at least 0.39 for eps <= 0.0040, and at most 0.5 * log2(1/(1-eps)) more bits (0.0072 for eps = 0.01) restore it beyond.

The declared experiments run this program in the organizer sandbox: bsrho-n18 (one attempt of the 256-lane search per trial at width 18, DP = low 2 bits zero) and proj-k0-w256 (2048 points of the K = 0 target at width 256 per trial, a pair when two digests agree in the low 21 bits). Each returns pairs whose complete 3-round digests agree in the stated low bits. They check the circuit, bookkeeping and recovery on the real target and give organizer-counted frequencies; not the cost or success probability at width 256. No outside code or library is used.

Nonuniform advice: two 256-bit words, 64 bytes, counted in the memory total, nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 6: the integer i = 10768619076 (34 bits, one word) and the input polarity vector PINS (one word, the output of the shipped climb, proof 3.6). P is the block with little-endian words w0 = i mod 2^32, w1 = i >> 32, w2..w15 = 0, and the program derives P and the chaining value from i. i is the first candidate of the shipped scan (proof.md Section 8, 7,721,099,878,210 operations, preprocessing_log2 = 33.5, a row of the ledger) with (A1 + B2) mod 2^32 = 0.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. f(x) = digest(P || 0^32 || x), the 3-round complete hash of the 128-byte message with the fixed first block P of proof.md Section 8 (the root compression of block 2 with chaining value CV = chain_value(P)), behaves as a random mapping on N = 2^256 points for everything the search evaluates: (a) for the inputs the search evaluates, the 256-bit outputs behave as uniform and independent values, so that two distinct evaluated inputs collide with probability 2^-256 (this entry uses no input difference and does not claim that none exists); (b) the iterates of f from the starts r + t (r a fresh uniform 256-bit word, t < 2^16) have the first-collision law of a random mapping (trails of length near 2^114.9 merge as independent random paths); (c) whether an iterate is a distinguished point (low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 142) is independent of (a) and (b) and has probability 142 / 2^122. Under H1 the success probability of the single attempt is at least 0.39 (proof.md Section 4).
heuristics.scope: The fixed target blake3-r3-prefix-v1, the fixed first block P, the fixed key m0..m7 = 0, the 2^128-scale evaluation of f along about 9400 trails of mean length 2^114.89 started from r + t, 256 trails at a time. Not claimed for other keys, other prefixes, other round counts, or evaluations beyond this scale.
heuristics.extrapolation: Declared and not proved. The full 256-bit functional graph, trails longer than 2^40 and 2^128 evaluations cannot be observed. Evidence run by this entry's own program: the organizer experiments bsrho-n18 (the 256-lane search at width 18, one attempt per trial; the organizer counts the trials that return a verified pair) and proj-k0-w256 (2048 points of the K = 0 target with prefix P at width 256 per trial; the organizer counts the trials whose point set contains a collision of a 21-bit projection), and the tests T1 to T3 that the program prints (proof.md Section 5). Extrapolation from widths up to 18 (search) and 21 projection bits at 2048 points (full width) to width 256 and 2^128 evaluations is by the premise only. A deficit eps in the pair-collision rate costs 0.5 * log2(1/(1-eps)) bits (0.0072 for eps = 0.01), listed in Limits.
heuristics.limitations: The full 256-bit functional graph, iterations above 2^40, and other keys are untested. The experiments show correctness of the program and no deviation at the sizes run (256 trials each; the standard deviation of a success frequency is about 0.03); they do not measure collision structure at 2^128 evaluations. The organizer reports the counts of returned pairs; the ideal-function control, the family-law runs and the other six projections are the program's own observations. A rate deficit eps of H1 (a) above 0.0040 lowers the success probability below 0.39 and is repaired by at most 0.5 * log2(1/(1-eps)) more bits of time.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. Under H1, the points lost at the halt and the events outside the birthday count are bounded as in proof.md Section 4: the sum of the ages of the 256 unfinished trails is at most 350 L except with probability 1e-6 (each age dominated by an exponential with mean L = 2^114.89); the number of cut trails is Poisson with mean 0.157, charged as 3.22e-04 of probability (a third cut is a halt); the expected number of colliding pairs inside one trail is at most 1.1e-04; a key false match has probability below 5e-12; the table-capacity abort has probability below 2^-41.9. The sum of these probabilities is below 4.37e-04.
heuristics.scope: The parameters of plan(256) in experiments/bsrho.py: 256 lanes, DP density 142 / 2^122, age cap 11 L, table of 10160 keys.
heuristics.extrapolation: Computations under H1 only (geometric trail lengths, memoryless DP events); the same formulas are implemented in plan(n) and loss(p) and the plan is exercised at n = 18 in the experiments.
heuristics.limitations: The 256 ages are treated as independent, each dominated by an exponential, under H1 (c); the cut-trail loss is bounded as a probability over the number of cut trails (Poisson) in proof.md Section 4 and costs 3.22e-04, inside the 1.65e-03 slack.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical premise of this entry. The cost model prices a 256-bit word RAM with loads and stores and fixes no register count; this entry declares R = 1,024 registers of 256 bits, counted as 32,768 bytes of memory, and charges every operation, load, store and register move. The main loop (one batch of 256 trails, 18904 operations: the 18866-operation generated step, a 35-operation stage-1 test and 3 loop operations) has no load, store or move because the generated line needs 771 registers (output plane j in the register of input plane j). The organizer's reference count C(r3) = 638 is used only as the unit. Every instruction is charged 36 bytes of code.
heuristics.scope: The loop body of one batch of 256 lanes, its stage-1 test and the handlers; table accesses, recovery, events and setup are charged at the stated bounds including loads and stores of their words.
heuristics.extrapolation: A machine with fewer than 771 registers would add loads and stores to every batch; proof.md 3.5 gives the cost (time_log2 125.0227 with 512 registers, 125.2382 with 256). The claim assumes the declared 1,024.
heuristics.limitations: The benchmark profile does not fix a register count; the declaration is this entry's own. The count 18866 is produced by the generator in the program and the register allocation by `allocate`; smaller files are priced by the program's Belady allocation of the straight line (an upper bound on what a better schedule needs).

heuristics.statement: Supporting, used by the score-critical claim. The target's message domain, quoted from the organizer profile field message_domain, is "Finite byte strings of bit length below 2^64." The attack outputs two 128-byte messages P || 0^32 || x and P || 0^32 || y, which are byte strings of that domain; the standard chunk rules for 128 bytes (one chunk, two blocks, flags 1 on block 1 and 10 on block 2) apply and are those of verifier/blake3.py. P is a fixed constant of the program, fixed before the attack by the bounded scan of proof.md Section 8 (program shipped, operations charged) for the one condition (A1 + B2) mod 2^32 = 0 on the chaining value of P; the attack does not depend on any other property of P.
heuristics.scope: The target blake3-r3-prefix-v1, messages of exactly 128 bytes whose first 64 bytes are P and whose bytes 64..95 are zero. Not claimed for other message lengths, other prefixes, or keyed or tree modes.
heuristics.extrapolation: None beyond the profile text: the claim relies on the profile accepting any finite byte string as a message. The claim does not apply to a reading of the domain that excludes 128-byte strings; the bit-sliced entry 0a9640ed (124.96822) makes a claim for 64-byte messages. The program's digest functions agree with verifier/blake3.py on 300 messages of this form (0 differences), and both organizer experiments recompute the digests of the 128-byte messages with the organizer's reference.
heuristics.limitations: The scan that found P is a one-time computation of 10,768,619,077 candidates with the shipped scan program (7,721,099,878,210 operations, a row of the ledger), stated as preprocessing_log2 = 33.5; P is retained as nonuniform advice of one word, and the polarity vector PINS (output of the shipped climb, proof 3.6, 24,959,503,800 operations, a ledger row, within preprocessing_log2 = 33.5) as a second word (together nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 6, counted in memory); its uniformity assumption (a random chaining value passes with probability 2^-32) is used only to describe the scan and is not used by the attack.
